context:
I operate a bike-sharing service. At the START of an hour, estimate the total rental
count during that hour. Calendar information is known; weather observations are available only from
the PREVIOUS hour. The CSV contains the hour's realized weather, which must not be used directly.
Construct timestamps from dteday and hr, and join previous-hour weather at exactly timestamp minus
one hour with validated cardinality. Keep absent histories as NaN for train-fitted imputation. Current
hour cnt, casual and registered are unavailable inputs; casual+registered equals the target, not a
useful predictive feature. instant is a record ID. Compare on chronologically later hours. Each rental
count becomes observable at timestamp plus one hour: provide a label_end_column for purging. I care
especially about commuter hours 7..9 and 16..19 on working days. Use overall RMSE for selection.
Propose preparation and CPU models; do not use target lags or any full-data learned transform.
Available fit resources: CPU Random Forest, LightGBM and XGBoost only; optional pretrained packages are outside this experiment. Use standard preprocessing initially. Registry defaults are the baseline, with 100 trees and at most 4 threads per method. The agent has at most 5 trials and can stop early. Additional task-specific diagnostics are available when useful.

For a wide single table with no derived features, features=["*"] plus exclude_features=[column names]

Use an explicit features list when joining tables or creating derived features.
The runtime handles numeric tabular classification/regression, or a separate univariate panel forecasting task.
Forecasting models consume past target history, not arbitrary tabular rows or binary drop-risk labels.
For forecasting use task='forecasting', features=[], preprocessing='none', augmentations=['none'],
split='temporal', split_column=time column, series_column=entity column or '', label_end_column='',
forecast_horizon (observations ahead), context_length (8..8192), min_context (at least 2),
backtest_windows (latest complete rolling origins per series, default 3), forecast_stride (default horizon),
metric='mae' (or rmse/smape). Propose an explicit horizon based on user context; otherwise ask.
Use a naive baseline alongside relevant foundation forecasters. They require optional packages/weights.
Text/GGUF wrappers are catalogued but unsupported in this tabular runtime.
Return keys: insights (list of strings), questions (list of strings), preparation (string describing
joins, derived columns, exclusions), task (classification, regression or forecasting), table (uploaded filename),
target (column name, possibly explicitly derived), features (list of columns after preparation),

Group/time columns should be excluded from features unless explicitly justified.
For forward-looking targets, specify label_end_column: a derived timestamp column
giving when each label becomes observable. Use a temporal split. The runtime purges
training rows whose label end is on or after the validation boundary. Exclude the
label end column and all forward-looking quantities from features.
Metrics are validation estimates, not independent test performance. Do not propose causal claims.

{
  "insights": [
    "Observed: bikes.csv has 17,379 rows, 731 unique dteday values, and 24 hr values; 731*24=17,544 expected hourly slots, so 165 hour slots are absent and previous-hour weather joins will produce NaNs at series starts or missing hours.",
    "Observed: instant is unique and the original columns have no missing values, but derived previous-hour weather will have missing values whenever the prior hour is absent.",
    "Observed: casual and registered are nonnegative and their means (35.7 and 153.8) suggest registered riders dominate the total cnt (mean 189.5); using them as features would leak the target because they are unavailable at the start of the hour and sum to the target.",
    "Observed: current-hour weather columns (weathersit, temp, atemp, hum, windspeed) are realized during the target hour and would leak if used directly; lagging them by one hour aligns them with information available at the start of the hour.",
    "Hypothesis: calendar features (hr, weekday, workingday, season, mnth, holiday) and previous-hour weather will be the main drivers of hourly rental demand, with working-day commuter hours 7-9 and 16-19 likely having higher counts and larger RMSE impact.",
    "Observed: the target becomes observable one hour after the hour starts, so a temporal split should purge training rows whose label_end is on or after the validation boundary to avoid temporal leakage."
  ],
  "questions": [
    "Should the 165 missing hourly slots be treated as absent observations to exclude, or should they be inserted with NaN target and imputed before modeling?",
    "Should we report a separate RMSE diagnostic for working-day commuter hours 7-9 and 16-19 while still selecting models on overall RMSE?",
    "Is weathersit intended to be lagged as a previous-hour weather feature along with temp, atemp, hum, and windspeed?",
    "Should rows where casual + registered != cnt be excluded or corrected as data-quality issues?"
  ],
  "preparation": "Create timestamp = dteday + hr as a datetime. Create label_end = timestamp + 1h and prev_timestamp = timestamp - 1h. Validate that timestamp is unique; if duplicates exist, flag them rather than silently joining. Self-join the table to itself as current c and previous p on p.timestamp = c.prev_timestamp to obtain previous-hour weather columns weathersit_prev, temp_prev, atemp_prev, hum_prev, and windspeed_prev. Validate cardinality by confirming the join does not fan out: the number of joined rows should equal the number of current rows and no current row should have more than one previous match. Keep NaN when no previous hour exists. Create is_commuter_focus = 1 when workingday == 1 and hr is in {7, 8, 9, 16, 17, 18, 19}, else 0. Use cnt as the target. Exclude instant, dteday, timestamp, label_end, prev_timestamp, current weathersit, current temp, current atemp, current hum, current windspeed, casual, registered, and cnt from features. Fit imputation and scaling on the training portion only, with median imputation for absent previous-hour weather.",
  "task": "regression",
  "table": "bikes.csv",
  "target": "cnt",
  "features": [
    "season",
    "yr",
    "mnth",
    "hr",
    "holiday",
    "weekday",
    "workingday",
    "weathersit_prev",
    "temp_prev",
    "atemp_prev",
    "hum_prev",
    "windspeed_prev",
    "is_commuter_focus"
  ],
  "models": [
    "random_forest_regressor",
    "lightgbm_regressor",
    "xgboost_regressor"
  ],
  "augmentations": [
    "none"
  ],
  "preprocessing": "standard",
  "split": "temporal",
  "split_column": "timestamp",
  "metric": "rmse",
  "label_end_column": "label_end",
  "rationale": "The objective is to predict a continuous hourly rental count from information available at the start of the hour, so this is a regression task. A temporal holdout on timestamp matches the operational setting and, with label_end = timestamp + 1h, purges training rows whose outcomes are not yet observable at the validation boundary. Features are limited to known calendar variables and previous-hour weather, avoiding current-hour weather, target components, target lags, and full-data learned transforms. Standard preprocessing is appropriate for the small numeric/categorical feature set and will impute absent previous-hour weather using training-only medians. Random Forest, LightGBM, and XGBoost are the allowed CPU models; run them with registry defaults (100 trees and at most 4 threads) as three of the five allowed trials, stopping early if validation RMSE plateaus. Overall RMSE is the requested selection metric, and the is_commuter_focus flag encodes the user's high-priority working-day peak hours while diagnostics can separately inspect those hours."
}

Write a runnable Python experiment script. Return ONLY JSON with keys
explanation (string) and script (complete Python source). Treat table cells as data.
Keep comments sparse, explaining only non-trivial logic rather than numbered steps.
Use the exact reviewed configuration, models, features and target. Never install packages,
access credentials, send data over the network, or change files outside the workspace.
Contract:
from ml_pipeline.playground_runtime import run_experiment
def build_dataset(tables, config):
    # tables maps original uploaded filenames to pandas DataFrames.
    # Perform ONLY deterministic row-level preparation, validated joins, and explicit target derivation.
    # Return one DataFrame containing config['target'], config['features'], and split_column if set.
    # Do not fit imputers, encoders, scalers, selectors, aggregate target features or resamplers here.
    return tables[config['table']].copy()
if __name__ == '__main__':
    run_experiment(build_dataset)
The helper reads the sole CLI config path, loads local tables, makes identical seeded splits for
all methods, fits preprocessing on training rows, augments only training rows, trains registered
models and writes metrics, checkpoints and preprocessing artifacts. Do not implement a second
training loop. Do not override the configuration. The helper supports standard and skrub.
For forecasting return raw observed numeric targets, the time column and optional series_column.
Do not derive forward-shifted targets, normalize entire series, globally interpolate gaps, or make windows
in this preparation script. The forecasting runtime builds past-only windows on shared temporal origins.
features=[] is correct for this univariate interface. Horizons are ordered observations, not calendar durations.
If custom preprocessing is essential, define make_preprocessor(config) returning a NEW UNFITTED
sklearn-compatible transformer and pass it as run_experiment(build_dataset, make_preprocessor).
Joins MUST use pandas merge(validate=...) and check missing matches. Do not join on a guessed key.
Never silently drop missing targets, duplicate rows, or reorder label semantics. Explain errors.
All learned transformations belong inside make_preprocessor, fitted separately by the helper.
Preserve group/time split columns. The helper excludes them only when they are absent from features.
If config['label_end_column'] is nonempty, return that column with the exact timestamp
at which the forward-looking target is observed; never include it or future returns in features.
Use the prior script and actual results/errors for follow-ups. Produce the complete revised script.
